quote: d. Ownership. Notwithstanding the license granted under section 2.1, TrueLink retains all of its ownership and license rights in the Interface.
rationale: The only ownership provision is one-directional: Section 2(d) confirms TrueLink retains ownership of the Interface (acceptable as Vendor background IP), but nothing in the Agreement confirms that Client retains all right, title and interest in Client Content, Client's Intellectual Property and the data it and its borrowers submit, and nothing addresses ownership of the results of the Support Services that Client pays for. The nearest support is confidentiality only (Sections 10(b) and 10(c), which deem "all results of the Hosting and Support Services" Client Proprietary Information) and a narrow termination-only statement in Section 13 that Client "shall retain full ownership of all domains associated with Client and Client Content" in case of discontinued Service. Confidential treatment and a termination-time carve-out are not ownership, and the Agreement gives Client no ownership of, or licence to, work product created for it, so it fails even the fallback (no perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free right to use, modify and sublicense deliverables). We have therefore inserted a reciprocal ownership clause at the preferred position, preserving TrueLink's platform rights and expressly subordinating our data ownership statement to the existing Section 8(d) licence so no conflict is created. Separately noted, not double-flagged here: the Section 8(d) licence permitting TrueLink to "resell, exploit" Credit Data is a licence rather than an assignment and is limited by the Non-Competition Agreement, so it is a data-use point rather than an ownership breach.
